### Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/13160
Originally posted by **freud14-tm** January 6, 2025 ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python from typing import Annotated, TypeAlias from fastapi import FastAPI, Header from pydantic import BaseModel app = FastAPI() class CommonHeaders(BaseModel): host: str save_data: bool if_modified_since: str | None = None traceparent: str | None = None x_tag: list[str] = [] CommonHeadersAnnotated: TypeAlias = Annotated[CommonHeaders, Header()] @app.get("/items/") async def read_items(headers: CommonHeadersAnnotated): return headers @app.get("/items2/") async def read_items2(x_prd_code: Annotated[str, Header()], headers: CommonHeadersAnnotated): return headers ``` ### Description There seems to be a few problems when using [Header Parameter Models](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/header-param-models/) as documented. The code above and the screenshots bellow show it. First, it seems that the Swagger UI doesn't convert underscores into dashes when using a Header Parameter Model. It works fine otherwise. Second, when using another header in the function, FastAPI interprets the parameter model as an object to be sent as a single header with the parameters as a comma-separated list instead of expecting the single parameters. ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f387f1d-e737-492a-98ae-752dafa7438b) ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30e5eaea-2d5f-4595-b989-46fb6bf89e00) ### Operating System Linux ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.115.6 ### Pydantic Version 2.10.4 ### Python Version 3.11.0 ### Additional Context _No response_

comments.body: I will not have time to look into this myself, but it would be good to have this fixed as one should be able to handle the headers correctly in Swagger, especially if there are - as in our case - proprietary headers added to the requests to be tested.
This is a feature request, not a bug. FastAPI doesn't support it yet.
Well, then it would be nice to have that included in the documentation, because we did it according to what's written there and ran straight into this problem.
Where in the documentation it uses `BaseModel` for headers?

https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/header-param-models/
If you combine that with the approach described here https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/header-params/ you get the problem.
Ah, then it's a bug. Sorry.

For the second part of the bug, I believe something like this would fix it:

Currently, in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`, for the function `_get_flat_fields_from_params`, if the length of `fields` is over one and there is a `BaseModel` in the second index (like in this issue), then that `BaseModel` will not be properly extracted:

```python
def _get_flat_fields_from_params(fields: List[ModelField]) -> List[ModelField]:
    if not fields:
        return fields
    first_field = fields[0]
    if len(fields) == 1 and lenient_issubclass(first_field.type_, BaseModel):
        fields_to_extract = get_cached_model_fields(first_field.type_)
        return fields_to_extract
    return fields
```

Changing it to this seems to fix the issue:

```python
def _get_flat_fields_from_params(fields: List[ModelField]) -> List[ModelField]:
    extracted_fields = []

    for field in fields:
        if lenient_issubclass(field.type_, BaseModel):
            fields_to_extract = get_cached_model_fields(field.type_)
            extracted_fields.extend(fields_to_extract)
        else:
            extracted_fields.append(field)

    return extracted_fields
```

Let me know if you'd like me to make a PR for this change.

@jpjacobpadilla thanks for looking at it! I think it would be good to treat that as soon as possible, so I'd appreciate you making a PR for it. @Kludex how about the first part of the bug (the underscores)?

Looking into the first part with the underscore issue seems to be there is no unpacking of the BaseModel in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` for the function `analyze_param` currently it just looks at the outer parameter and replaces any underscores in it's name without inspecting if the parameter is actually a model.
Added in some very awful code to just verify what happens if we unpack the fields and got the underscores working correctly just below ln 495 in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` in the `analyze_param` function
```python
        if getattr(field_info, "convert_underscores", None) and lenient_issubclass(field.type_, BaseModel):
            fields = _get_flat_fields_from_params([field])
            for flat_field in fields:
                flat_field.field_info.alias = flat_field.name.replace("_", "-")
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61374d89-bf2e-420f-92ee-9e1f513c3899)

Yes, there definitely needs to be an additional conversion of the parameter names if they are sent from Swagger. I did this myself using a middleware modifying the incoming headers, but that is a pretty awful hack, too. Would be nice to fix it in the source code itself.
I'll look into cleaning up the code to fit more within the `analyze_param` function and then could look into creating a PR for it
@tiangolo can these be integrated into an upcoming version?

Thanks for the discussion, everyone!

Let's split this into two things.

The first, handling correctly `convert_underscores`, this is a bug, let's keep this issue for that. It should have been handled in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/13515 🎉 

This will be released in the next version, `0.115.12`, in the next hours.

The new docs: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/header-param-models/#forbid-extra-headers

---

About having a model alongside another parameter, this would be a feature request, better in a new discussion.

I'm also not sure about it, because it would behave differently from a body parameter alongside a body model. So I would have to think about that feature some more first. For now, when using a Pydantic model for headers, only one model per path operation is supported.

Anyway, feel free to create a new discussion question with the feature request. 🤓
I can confirm that the underscore conversion now works as expected, thanks for integrating this.

As for the second part, there is no urgend need on our side to have it fixed as soon as possible as we can use single header parameters instead of models, therefore I relinquish to create a new discussion for the time being and will close this issue, but if someone feels the need to continue this, feel free.

title: Header parameter and model handling does not work as expected
